sections.heading: Start with a story or engineering evidence
text: A PM brings the story. An engineer can bring an existing flow, an HLD, or trace evidence. Both create the same reviewable project.

panels.title: On screen · choose your conversation
panels.alt: Flowview setup: Copy & paste keeps the conversation in your coding agent’s app.
panels.caption: Copy & paste keeps the conversation in your agent app.

steps.text: Start with a customer story: actor, goal, major steps, and exceptions. No graph vocabulary is required.
Or start from an existing engineering flow, an HLD, or a Honeycomb trace. Claude asks for missing details and keeps evidence distinct from assumptions.
The draft becomes a Flowview spec plus a coverage ledger. The ledger records questions, decisions, evidence, and open work.
Flowview renders the story so people can inspect the steps, system relationships, and missing coverage before accepting an update.
Click the Next · Claude arrow card to see how a new diagram begins with Claude Code.

sections.heading: Work with Claude in its own conversation
text: Flowview handles the shared project and preview. Your questions, replies and permissions stay in the external Claude Code conversation.

steps.text: Choose New Connection → Start a new diagram with an agent. The workbench asks where the conversation will happen and where the diagram will live.
Select an empty folder. Flowview prepares the connection instructions and authoring kit there. Review the full instructions before copying them.
Paste the setup instructions into Claude Code. Claude verifies the exact folder, reads the packaged guidance, and works with normal file permissions.

log.text: I found the folder and will draft the worksheet first.

steps.text: Claude turns the story into steps, nodes and edges, while recording assumptions and open questions in the ledger. This panel is illustrative, not a live transcript.

log.text: What should happen when the payment is declined?
Keep the cart; let the customer retry.

log.text: The preview is ready in Flowview. Please review it before committing the update.

sections.heading: Preview, correct, then accept the pair
text: Each proposal carries a spec and coverage ledger together. A human compares the candidate with the accepted project, then accepts or requests corrections.

panels.title: On screen · preview before committing
panels.alt: Actual Flowview review UI with a seeded checkout example: compare Proposed / Current, then Commit update or Discard update.
panels.caption: Compare Proposed and Current, then commit or discard the update.

steps.text: A request captures the message, selected items, view, path, step, and detail level. Copy alone does not silently send it to Claude.
Claude edits the seeded candidate spec and ledger. The accepted files remain untouched until a person approves the proposal.
Preview Agent Updates renders the proposal. Compare Current and Proposed, inspect change highlights, and expand the coverage ledger when needed.
Choose Commit update only after review. Flowview saves the spec and ledger together; one Undo can restore the prior pair.
If the proposal is wrong or conflicts with a newer edit, discard or copy feedback. Claude reconciles the current pair and submits a new proposal.
Claude uses the feedback and latest accepted revision to prepare corrected candidates. The new proposal still needs a fresh human review.
Review the corrected Current and Proposed states. An earlier approval cannot be reused after a change.
The accepted pair is saved in the diagram folder. Continue to Resume to pick up the same project later.

sections.heading: Resume the project, then make the next change
text: The folder preserves the accepted story and coverage. The agent connection is temporary; reconnect before continuing.

steps.text: Choose Continue an existing agent build, then select the SAME diagram folder used before.
Flowview restores the saved spec, coverage ledger and workbench history. An open draft is kept in Earlier drafts; old pending work is not replayed.
Reconnect using Copy & paste. Continue the earlier Claude conversation when available; in a new session, provide the current setup and project context.
Describe the next change. Claude reads the current project, prepares candidates, and submits another proposal for human review.
Local acceptance is separate from publishing. Continue to Backstage to see how reviewed diagrams become discoverable.

sections.heading: Discover diagrams on the service or API page
text: Company pattern: approved GitHub specs are discovered through explicit entity bindings. The screenshot shows the actual plugin in a fictional local preview.

steps.text: After local acceptance, publish the spec and ledger through the company repository review process. Workbench Commit update does not make a Git commit.
The company Backstage integration reads the approved snapshot from GitHub. The company fork hosts the static Workbench; it does not host a diagram API.
